e.title: **一条热带气旋巨灾建模链，从风暴轨迹到损失、再从一百年历史轨迹到随机事件集**：仓库 `christianwirths/NatCat`——**⭐ 九段链条**逐段成模块**（**数据 → 轨迹 → 致灾因子 → 脆弱性 → 暴露 → 损失 → 随机事件集 → 财务模块 → 出图**）**；**⭐ 而其中**暴露那一段**可以调用已收录的 [[climada]]**（**逐字** `geo = ["cartopy", "climada"]`**）**；**⚠️ 自述 0.1.0**、**★1**
e.title_en: An open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling chain that runs from storm track to loss and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set, with each link of the chain as its own module and the exposure link able to call an existing open catastrophe-model platform as an optional dependency.
e.title_hk: **一條熱帶氣旋巨災建模鏈，從風暴軌跡到損失、再從一百年歷史軌跡到隨機事件集**：倉庫 `christianwirths/NatCat`——**⭐ 九段鏈條**逐段成模組**（**資料 → 軌跡 → 致災因子 → 脆弱性 → 暴露 → 損失 → 隨機事件集 → 財務模組 → 出圖**）**；**⭐ 其中**暴露那一段**可以調用已收錄的 [[climada]]**（**逐字** `geo = ["cartopy", "climada"]`**）**；**⚠️ 自述 0.1.0**、**★1**
e.summary: **natcat-tc-modelling**（`christianwirths/NatCat`，**包名逐字** `natcat` **0.1.0**）**是一个**开放的热带气旋巨灾建模框架****——**README 逐字自述**「**An open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling framework: from storm track to loss, and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set with exceedance-probability curves.**」**。**本次实测**：**创建 2025-12-09、最后推送 2026-09-09**、**★1**、**主语言 Jupyter Notebook**；**许可 MIT**（**`LICENSE` 逐字** `MIT License`／`Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Wirths`**）**；**tarball 枚举 154 条路径**（**11 个测试文件、**3 个 notebook、**`docs/` 下** `api/` **10 页与** `methodology/` **5 页**）**。**⭐⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**下游：把上游当成引擎与输入**」**——**它把已收录的 [[climada]] 当作**可选的暴露生成后端****（**逐字** `geo = ["cartopy", "climada"]`**）**，**并与 [[tcrm]]、[[ibtracs]]、[[spatialrisk]]、[[openquake-engine]] 同属巨灾建模一侧**。**⭐⭐⭐ 三处最值得看**：**① **它把「建模链」**拆成九个可单独替换的模块****（**数据、轨迹、致灾因子、脆弱性、暴露、损失、随机事件集、财务、出图**）**——**⭐ 即**链条上的每一段都可以被别人换掉**；**② **随机事件集用**经验马尔可夫轨迹生成器**，**在一九〇〇至二〇二〇年大西洋 best track 上标定****；**③ **`docs/methodology/limitations.md` 单独立页列局限**。**⚠️ 本次未运行任何一步、**未做与其它巨灾平台的对比**。
e.summary_hk: **natcat-tc-modelling**（`christianwirths/NatCat`，**包名逐字** `natcat` **0.1.0**）**是一個**開放的熱帶氣旋巨災建模框架****——**README 逐字自述**「**An open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling framework: from storm track to loss, and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set with exceedance-probability curves.**」**。**本次實測**：**建立 2025-12-09、最後推送 2026-09-09**、**★1**、**Jupyter Notebook**；**許可 MIT**；**tarball 列舉 154 條路徑**（**11 個測試檔、**3 個 notebook、**`docs/api/` 10 頁與** `docs/methodology/` **5 頁**）**。**⭐⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**下游：把上游當成引擎與輸入**」**——**它把已收錄的 [[climada]] 當作**可選的暴露生成後端****（**逐字** `geo = ["cartopy", "climada"]`**）**。**⭐⭐⭐ 三處最值得看**：**① **把「建模鏈」**拆成九個可單獨替換的模組**；**② **隨機事件集用**經驗馬爾可夫軌跡生成器**，**在一九〇〇至二〇二〇年大西洋 best track 上標定****；**③ **`docs/methodology/limitations.md` 單獨立頁列局限**。**⚠️ 本次未運行任何一步、未做與其它巨災平台的對比**。
e.summary_en: The repository NatCat, distributed under the package name natcat at version 0.1.0, **is an open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling framework**, described verbatim as running from storm track to loss, and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set with exceedance-probability curves. **Measured this round**: **created 2025-12-09**, **last pushed 2026-09-09**, **one star**, primarily Jupyter notebooks, **licensed MIT** with a licence file naming the author and year, and **154 paths in the extracted archive**, including eleven test files, three notebooks, and a documentation site with ten API pages and five methodology pages. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the downstream using the upstream as an engine and an input, because it treats an existing open catastrophe-platform package as an optional exposure-generation backend** and sits on the catastrophe-modelling side alongside pooled entries for tropical-cyclone risk modelling, historical best-track data, an exposure data service and an open seismic engine. **Three things are worth reading**: the modelling chain **is split into nine separately replaceable modules** covering data, tracks, hazards, vulnerability, exposure, loss, the stochastic event set, financial metrics and plotting, so any single link can be swapped by someone else; the stochastic event set **uses an empirical Markov track generator calibrated on Atlantic best tracks from 1900 to 2020**; and **limitations get their own methodology page**. **Nothing was run this round, and no comparison against other catastrophe platforms was made.**
e.body:
**NatCat**（GitHub 仓库 `christianwirths/NatCat`，**发行包名逐字** `natcat`）**是一个**开放的热带气旋巨灾建模框架****，**README 逐字自述**「**An open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling framework: from storm track to loss, and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set with exceedance-probability curves.**」**。**本次实测**：**创建 2025-12-09、最后推送 2026-09-09**、**★1**、**主语言 Jupyter Notebook**；**许可 MIT**（**`LICENSE` 逐字** `MIT License`／`Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Wirths`**）**；**tarball 枚举 154 条路径**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**下游：把上游当成引擎与输入**」**。

**可核实信息（均 README、`pyproject.toml` 与文件清单实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它把整条建模链拆成**九个模块**，**并逐段说明每段干什么**——**本次实测的九段与自述**：**① `natcat.data`——**读 NHC 的 ATCF B-deck 与 A-deck**，**并可按需下载历史存档**；**② `natcat.tracks`——**轨迹处理**；**③ `natcat.hazards`——**Rankine 涡旋风场**，**且把**移动不对称性**算进去**；**④ `natcat.vulnerability`——**按建筑类型给的 S 形脆弱性曲线**；**⑤ `natcat.exposure`——**合成暴露或调用其它模型给的真实暴露****（**⭐ 见下**）**；**⑥ `natcat.loss`——**损失计算**；**⑦ `natcat.stochastic`——**经验马尔可夫轨迹生成器**，**在**一九〇〇至二〇二〇年大西洋 best track**上标定**；**⑧ `natcat.financial`——**AEP 与 OEP**，**尾部用广义帕累托分布**；**⑨ `natcat.plotting`——**出图**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处**：**「**建模链**」**不是**一个脚本从头跑到尾，**而是**九段**，**每段**有名字、**每段**可以单独替换**——**⭐ 即**别人想换掉脆弱性曲线时，**不必动你的轨迹生成器**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它把**暴露**这一段交给**已收录的平台**——**本次实测** `pyproject.toml` **中逐字有一条可选依赖**：**`geo = ["cartopy", "climada"]`**，**而 [[climada]] 已在本站收录**；**README 亦把 CLIMADA 的 **LitPop** 列为暴露的一种来源**。**⭐ 即**「**我不自己造暴露数据**」**这句话被写进了依赖声明**——**⭐ 这与本站第 337 轮「**没有任何东西站在单一来源上**」同向**：**同一条链上，**致灾因子自己算**，**暴露可以借别人的**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 随机事件集是**经验**的，**且标定窗口被写明**——**逐字为**「**empirical Markov track generator calibrated on 1900–2020 Atlantic best tracks**」**；**⭐ 本词条认为这一句有三处可抄**：**① **是「**经验**」而非**参数化**（**即从历史轨迹里学转移，**而不是假设一个风暴生成模型**）**；**② **标定数据被指明**（**大西洋 best track**）**；**③ **标定窗口被写明**（**一九〇〇至二〇二〇**）**——**⭐ 而窗口一旦写明，**读者就能自己判断**它是否够长、**是否跨了气候 regime 变化**。**⭐⭐ ④ 它把**局限**单独立页**——**文件清单实测** `docs/methodology/` **下 5 页，**其中一页逐字为** `limitations.md`**。**⭐ 本词条认为这与本站第 334 轮「**边界即清单**」、第 341 轮「**三种缺席**」同向**：**局限不是散在正文里的一句话，**而是**一个有名有姓的页面**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 依赖与工具链被写明，**且分开了「**必需**」与「**可选**」****——**本次实测** `pyproject.toml`：**包名** `natcat` **0.1.0**、**`requires-python` 逐字为** `>=3.10`；**关键词里含** `insurance`**；**必需依赖** `numpy`、`pandas`、`scipy`、`matplotlib`、`requests`、`tqdm`、`beautifulsoup4`、`scikit-learn`、`global-land-mask`；**可选依赖** `geo`（**`cartopy` ＋ `climada`**）；**开发依赖** `pytest` ＋ `ruff`；**文档依赖** `mkdocs-material`、`mkdocstrings`、`mkdocs-jupyter`。**⭐ 即**「**要跑核心链不需要装地理库**」**这件事**是被**声明**出来的**，**而不是**靠读者去试**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 过程留痕可数**：**测试文件 11 个**；**notebook 3 个**；**文档站** `docs/` **含** `api/` **10 页**（**对应九个模块加总览**）**与** `methodology/` **5 页**；**README 上挂着 CI 徽章，**而该徽章指向的分支逐字为** `dev/refactor-v1`**——**⭐ 本词条如实指出**：**「**主分支**」与「**CI 徽章指向的分支**」**两者本次**未分别核实**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[climada]]、[[climada-petals]] 覆盖开放巨灾平台**，**[[pyincore]] 覆盖社区韧性**，**[[openquake-engine]] 覆盖地震**，**[[tcrm]] 覆盖热带气旋风险建模**，**[[hazus]] 覆盖美国损失估计**，**[[noaa-inundation-mapping]]、[[gdacs]] 覆盖灾害数据**，**[[ibtracs]] 覆盖历史轨迹**，**[[gem-global-exposure-model]]、[[spatialrisk]] 覆盖暴露**，**[[pyextremes]]、[[mev]]、[[extremes]] 覆盖极值统计**，**[[oasislmf]]、[[oasis-piwind]]、[[ods-open-exposure-data]] 覆盖开放损失建模平台**——**⭐ 而本条补上的是**「**九个模块拼成一条链 ＋ 随机事件集用经验马尔可夫生成 ＋ 依赖里写明谁能替换谁**」这一形态**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[tcrm]]、[[climada]]、[[ibtracs]] 应当并读**——**它们分别给**热带气旋风险建模**、**开放平台与暴露**、**历史轨迹**；**⭐ 而对本词条项目最有借鉴的两点**：**① 一条链**按段命名**，**段与段之间只通过数据接口相连**；**② 凡是**借来的东西**（**暴露、**地理库**）**都在依赖声明里**写明是可选**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次没有运行该项目任何一步**（**未装依赖、**未跑 pytest、**未跑任何 notebook、**未生成任何 AEP 或 OEP 曲线**），**故**不主张**其风场、**脆弱性曲线、**损失计算**或**尾部分布**的任何数值结果**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未读其**方法学页面正文****——**本次只看到** `docs/methodology/` **下 5 页**与** `docs/api/` **下 10 页的存在与文件名**；**⭐ 未读** `limitations.md` **的内容**，**故**本词条**只主张**该页存在**，**不主张**它列了哪些局限**。**⚠️ 本条目最需后续核实的一处**。**③ ⚠️ 未核对 README 所述九段与源码目录是否一一对应**（**总路径 154 条为实测**，**但**模块内部的实现本次**未逐文件读**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核实「**一九〇〇至二〇二〇年大西洋 best track**」**这一标定窗口的实际取数范围**（**未读** `natcat/data` **的实现**，**也未访问 NHC 存档页**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实**「**按建筑类型给的 S 形脆弱性曲线**」**的参数来源****（**⭐ 即**未确认它是**从文献取值**、**从数据拟合**、还是**作者假设**）**——**⭐ 本词条如实指出**：**这一处直接决定损失一侧的可信度**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未与 [[tcrm]]、**[[climada]]、**[[openquake-engine]] 做任何代码或结果层面的比较**；**本条不主张 NatCat 优于或劣于其中任何一个**。**⑦ ⚠️ 未核实版本 0.1.0 是否已发布到 PyPI**（**⭐ 本次只读** `pyproject.toml` **中的版本号**）**。**⑧ ⚠️ 许可为 MIT（`LICENSE` 存在并读到两行**）**，**未读正文**；**⚠️ 并如实提示**：**CLIMADA 与 cartopy 各自另有许可**，**把 NatCat 用于交付物前**须分别看**。**⑨ ⚠️ 创建 2025-12-09 在解冻窗口之外、推送 2026-09-09 在窗口之内**——**本次按惯例把这一处写在这里**：**本条的缺口是「**把巨灾建模链逐段拆成模块 ＋ 暴露段显式接受外来引擎 ＋ 随机事件集写明经验标定窗口**」这一形态此前池内没有对应物**。**⑩ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 并如实提示**：**该框架 0.1.0、★1、**未经本站任何验证**，**不得**用于任何真实承保、**定价或资本计量**。

## 同类工具
[[uclfitter]]、[[wildfire-forecasting]]、[[alpaca-oasis-runner]]、[[apac-catastrophe-monitor]]

形脆弱性曲線**）、`natcat.exposure`（**合成暴露或調用其它模型給的真實暴露**）、`natcat.loss`、`natcat.stochastic`（**經驗馬爾可夫軌跡生成器，**在一九〇〇至二〇二〇年大西洋 best track 上標定**）、`natcat.financial`（**AEP 與 OEP，**尾部用廣義帕累托分布**）、`natcat.plotting`。**⭐ 本詞條認為這是本輪最值得抄的一處**：「**建模鏈**」**不是**一個腳本從頭跑到尾，**而是**九段**，**每段**有名字、**可以單獨替換**——**⭐ 即**別人想換掉脆弱性曲線時，**不必動你的軌跡生成器**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它把**暴露**這一段交給**已收錄的平台**——**本次實測** 輪「**沒有任何東西站在單一來源上**」同向**：**致災因子自己算，**暴露可以借別人的**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 隨機事件集是**經驗**的，**且標定窗口被寫明**——**逐字為**「**empirical Markov track generator calibrated on 1900–2020 Atlantic best tracks**」**——**⭐ 這與本站第 334 輪「**邊界即清單**」同向**：**局限不是散在正文裡的一句話，**而是**一個有名有姓的頁面**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 依賴分開了「**必需**」與「**可選**」****——**本次實測** `pyproject.toml`：**包名** `natcat` **0.1.0**、**`requires-python` 逐字為** `>=3.10`；**關鍵詞含** `insurance`**；**必需依賴** `numpy`、`pandas`、`scipy`、`matplotlib`、`requests`、`tqdm`、`beautifulsoup4`、`scikit-learn`、`global-land-mask`；**可選** `geo`（**`cartopy` ＋ `climada`**）；**開發** `pytest` ＋ `ruff`；**文檔** `mkdocs-material`、`mkdocstrings`、`mkdocs-jupyter`。**⭐ 即**「**要跑核心鏈不需要裝地理庫**」**是被**聲明**出來的**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 過程留痕可數**：**測試檔 11 個**、**notebook 3 個**、`docs/api/` **10 頁**、`docs/methodology/` **5 頁**；**README 的 CI 徽章指向的分支逐字為** `dev/refactor-v1`**——**⭐ 如實指出**：**「**主分支**」與「**CI 徽章指向的分支**」**兩者本次**未分別核實**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 與池內條目的關係**：[[climada]]、[[climada-petals]]、[[tcrm]]、[[pyincore]]、[[openquake-engine]]、[[hazus]]、[[noaa-inundation-mapping]]、[[gdacs]]、[[ibtracs]]、[[gem-global-exposure-model]]、[[spatialrisk]]、[[pyextremes]]、[[mev]]、[[extremes]]、[[oasislmf]]、[[oasis-piwind]]、[[ods-open-exposure-data]]——**⭐ 而本條補上的是**「**九個模組拼成一條鏈 ＋ 隨機事件集用經驗馬爾可夫生成 ＋ 依賴裡寫明誰能替換誰**」這一形態**。

**對 RIAA**：**本條與 [[tcrm]]、[[climada]]、[[ibtracs]] 應當並讀**——**⭐ 兩點最值得借鑑**：**① 一條鏈**按段命名**，**段與段之間只通過資料介面相連**；**② 凡是**借來的東西**都在依賴聲明裡**寫明是可選**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次沒有運行該專案任何一步**，**不主張**其風場、**脆弱性曲線、**損失計算**或**尾部分布**的任何數值結果**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未讀其**方法學頁面正文****——**只看到** 5 頁方法學與 10 頁 API **的存在與檔名**；**⭐ 未讀** `limitations.md` **的內容**，**只主張**該頁存在**。**⚠️ 本條目最需後續核實的一處**。**③ ⚠️ 未核對 README 所述九段與原始碼目錄是否一一對應**。**④ ⚠️ 未核實標定窗口的實際取數範圍**（**未讀** `natcat/data` **實現，**未訪問 NHC 存檔頁**）**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核實脆弱性曲線的**參數來源****（**是**文獻取值**、**資料擬合**、**還是**作者假設**）**——**⭐ 這一處直接決定損失一側的可信度**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未與 [[tcrm]]、**[[climada]]、**[[openquake-engine]] 做任何比較**；**不主張本專案優於或劣於其中任何一個**。**⑦ ⚠️ 未核實 0.1.0 是否已發佈到 PyPI**。**⑧ ⚠️ 許可為 MIT，未讀正文**；**⚠️ CLIMADA 與 cartopy 各自另有許可**，**用於交付物前須分別看**。**⑨ ⚠️ 建立 2025-12-09 在解凍窗口之外、推送 2026-09-09 在窗口之內**——**本條的缺口是「把巨災建模鏈逐段拆成模組＋暴露段顯式接受外來引擎＋隨機事件集寫明經驗標定窗口」這一形態此前池內沒有對應物**。**⑩ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⚠️ 0.1.0、★1、未經本站任何驗證**，**不得**用於任何真實承保、**定價或資本計量**。

e.body_en:
NatCat, on GitHub as christianwirths/NatCat and distributed under the package name natcat, **is an open tropical-cyclone catastrophe-modelling framework**, described verbatim as running from storm track to loss, and from a century of historical tracks to a stochastic event set with exceedance-probability curves. **Measured this round**: **created 2025-12-09**, **last pushed 2026-09-09**, **one star**, primarily Jupyter notebooks, **licensed MIT** with a licence file naming the author and year, and **154 paths in the extracted archive**. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the downstream using the upstream as an engine and an input.**

**Verified information, all measured from the README, the packaging metadata and the file listing**: **first, the whole modelling chain is split into nine modules with a stated role for each** — a data module that reads the National Hurricane Center ATCF B-deck and A-deck formats and can download historical archives on demand; a track module; a hazard module implementing a Rankine vortex wind field with motion asymmetry included; a vulnerability module giving sigmoid curves by construction type; an exposure module that is either synthetic or borrowed from another model; a loss module; a stochastic module holding an empirical Markov track generator calibrated on Atlantic best tracks from 1900 to 2020; a financial module computing average and occurrence exceedance probabilities with a generalised-Pareto tail; and a plotting module. **This entry considers that the most copyable idea of the round: the chain is not one script that runs from top to bottom, but nine named segments, each replaceable on its own, so somebody who wants a different vulnerability curve does not have to touch the track generator.** **Second, the exposure link is handed to an already pooled platform**: the packaging metadata declares an optional dependency group named geo holding cartopy and the pooled open catastrophe-platform package, and the README lists that platform LitPop product as one exposure source. **The sentence that says the project does not build its own exposure data is written into the dependency declaration**, which points the same way as a standing project principle that nothing should stand on a single source: on one and the same chain the hazard is computed here while the exposure may be borrowed. **Third, the stochastic event set is empirical and its calibration window is written down**: verbatim, an empirical Markov track generator calibrated on Atlantic best tracks from 1900 to 2020. **Three details are worth copying: it is empirical rather than parametric, meaning transitions are learned from historical tracks rather than assumed from a storm-generation model; the calibration data is named; and the calibration window is stated, which lets a reader judge whether the window is long enough and whether it spans a change of climate regime.** **Fourth, limitations get a dedicated page**: the methodology documentation directory holds five pages, one of which is a limitations page. **A limitation is therefore not a sentence buried in the body text but a page with a name**, which points the same way as standing project principles that boundaries should be lists and that absences should be named. **Fifth, dependencies are stated and split between required and optional**: the package is at version 0.1.0, requires Python at or above the stated floor, carries insurance among its keywords, requires numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, requests, tqdm, beautifulsoup4, scikit-learn and a global land mask, offers cartopy and the pooled catastrophe platform as an optional geo group, and adds pytest and ruff for development plus a material documentation theme, a docstring extractor and a notebook plugin for docs. **That the core chain can be run without installing geographic libraries is therefore declared rather than left for the reader to discover.** **Sixth, the process leaves countable traces**: eleven test files, three notebooks, ten API documentation pages and five methodology pages, with a CI badge whose target branch is named as a development refactor branch; **this entry states plainly that the default branch and the branch the badge points at were not separately verified**. **Seventh, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover open catastrophe platforms and their extensions, community resilience, seismic risk, tropical-cyclone risk modelling, United States loss estimation, disaster data feeds, historical tracks, global exposure models, extreme-value statistics and open loss-modelling platforms, **and this entry supplies a nine-module chain whose stochastic event set is empirically generated and whose dependencies state which link can be replaced by what**.

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside the pooled tropical-cyclone risk modeller, the pooled open catastrophe platform and the pooled historical track dataset**, which respectively supply cyclone risk modelling, an open platform with exposure generation, and historical tracks; **two practices transfer directly: name the links in a chain so that segments connect only through data interfaces, and declare anything borrowed — exposure, geographic libraries — as an optional dependency**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no step of the project was run** — no dependency installation, no test suite, no notebook and no exceedance-probability curve — **so no numerical result for its wind field, vulnerability curves, loss calculation or tail distribution is claimed**. **Second, no methodology page body was read**: only the existence and filenames of the five methodology pages and the ten API pages were observed, and **the limitations page content was not read, so this entry claims only that the page exists and not what limitations it lists**; **this is the item most in need of later verification**. **Third, the README nine-module description was not checked against the source tree one by one**, the total of 154 paths being what was measured. **Fourth, the actual data range behind the stated calibration window was not verified**, since the data module implementation was not read and no archive page was visited. **Fifth, the provenance of the vulnerability curve parameters was not verified** — whether they come from literature, from a fit, or from the author assumptions — **and this entry states plainly that this point directly determines how far the loss side can be trusted**. **Sixth, no code-level or result-level comparison against other pooled catastrophe tools was made, and this entry claims neither superiority nor inferiority to any of them.** **Seventh, whether version 0.1.0 has been published to a package index was not verified**, only the version number in the packaging metadata being read. **Eighth, the licence is MIT and its text was not read, and this entry notes that the optional geographic and catastrophe-platform dependencies carry their own licences, which must be checked separately before any deliverable use. Ninth, the creation date of 2025-12-09 is outside the thaw window while the push of 2026-09-09 is inside it**, and following the project convention of naming the gap, **the gap here is that a catastrophe modelling chain split segment by segment, with the exposure link explicitly accepting a foreign engine and a stochastic event set carrying a stated empirical calibration window, had no counterpart in the pool. Tenth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11, and states plainly that a version 0.1.0 project with one star and no independent verification by this site must not be used for any real underwriting, pricing or capital calculation.**
